base_member_text: [L36,L42-L58] (LOW/incomplete-validation) byteSizesOK never checks EightByteInt availability or bit size despite claiming to validate the module's selected integer kinds.
audit_member_text: [L36,L51-L58] (MED/kind-validation) byteSizesOK never validates EightByteInt, so it can report success when the advertised eight-byte integer kind is unavailable or has a different width.

adversarial.rationale: The standalone byteSizesOK function omits EightByteInt and can incorrectly endorse an unavailable or non-eight-byte selection, but this is a LOW portability-validation omission. In a complete netCDF-module build an unavailable kind is already rejected by declarations such as netcdf_expanded.f90:57, so a successfully built ordinary bundled library cannot reach the claimed unavailable-kind case.
